text:
alert-bot: [ALERT] EUW2 hosted GPU pool 'pool-eu-highmem' p95 queue latency spiked to 6.2s, admission control engaged, automatic fallback routing to eus3 triggered. Prom threshold: queue_p95 > 5s for 3m. :warning:
maria: seeing the same on the dashboard, Grafana panel 'pool_eu_highmem/queue_latency' shows a sharp ramp at 14:12UTC, correlates with a sudden surge in embedding jobs from acct:search-team.
sam: are we seeing image warmup or KV cache miss storms? any K8s node churn?
jia: kube events look clean, no scale-downs at the same time. I can see spike in avg-seqlen for those requests, batching probably hit a bad path.
andrew: FYI cost signal also ticked up ~12% for that pool between 14:10-14:20. Might be cross-tenant burst + small batch sizes.
maria: quick triage: queue length up, admission throttle active; fallback produced higher tail latency for some customers. Can we roll a targeted canary to reduce batch size or enable prefix-KV caching for embeddings?
sam: short-term: increase pool headroom by allocating 4 reserved instances from EUW2-spare (if available). Long-term: we need a playbook to detect request-shape spikes and apply per-route batching hints.
jia: checking spare capacity... EUW2 spare has 2 nodes free, eus3 has room. Ops API shows reserved pool depleted earlier today due to a Dedicated onboarding test.
alert-bot: tied alert details: {"pool":"pool-eu-highmem","p95_queue_ms":"6200","throttle_rate":"0.32","fallback_ratio":"0.14"} (raw metrics link: https://grafana.redwood/pool-eu-highmem?from=now-1h)
andrew: can we temporarily relax eviction thresholds so WarmUp images don't get evicted under pressure? That would lower cold-starts. Risk: higher cost. Thoughts?
maria: agree for short window. I'll open a quick PR to bump eviction TTL to 30m in EUW2 autoscaler config and add a guard so it auto-reverts in 30m.
sam: also adding an alert to catch request-seq-length spikes per-customer (new rule: seqlen_95pct > 1024 for 2m) so we can auto-tag traffic and apply routing policies.
jia: creating a dashboard snapshot and saving to the incident channel. Putting a playbook draft in the runbooks repo: steps -> 1) confirm spare nodes -> 2) allocate reserved -> 3) relax eviction TTL -> 4) apply per-route batching hints -> 5) monitor p95 queue -> 6) rollback.
andrew: will notify sales for impacted accounts. maria can you drive the PR?
maria: on it. tagging sam and jia for review. will post PR link when ready. :thumbsup:
sam: if PR approved, I'll coordinate with infra to move 2 nodes from eus3 back after traffic subsides to avoid ongoing cost.
jia: note for follow-up: add synthetic load test focused on embedding single-shot bursts to our chaos suite so we detect these earlier.
alert-bot: ALERT resolved at 14:34UTC — p95 queue returned to 1.1s after reserve allocation and eviction tweak. Closing loop: incident -> playbook draft saved -> PR opened: https://git.redwood/runbooks/pulls/45
maria: thanks both. I'll push a shorter-term eval to Redwood Optimize to see if quantization/packing can cut token cost for these workloads.
andrew: leaving notes for next retro: make sure Dedicated onboarding tests don't consume reserve during business hours.
sam: filing that ops policy ticket now.
maria: great thread — tagging @oncall for postmortem tomorrow. :eyes:
